rules.title: AI agent hooks or auto-approved tools
rules.summary: AI agent hooks and auto-approved tools: `.claude/settings*.json`, `.cursor/hooks.json`, `.mcp.json`, `.cursor/mcp.json`, `.vscode/mcp.json`.

reasons.hooks: Project settings define hooks that an AI coding agent runs automatically.
reasons.autoApprove: Project settings let an AI coding agent run any shell command without asking.
reasons.mcpAutoEnable: Project settings enable every MCP server in the repository without asking.
reasons.mcpServer: A project MCP configuration starts a local command when an AI agent loads the repository.

rules.why: AI coding agents read project-level configuration. Hooks and MCP servers are commands that run when the agent starts or uses a tool, and broad auto-approval lets injected instructions run shell commands unchecked.

references.title: VS Code Workspace Trust

rules.title: Font file is not a font
rules.summary: A file with a font extension whose bytes are not a real font (checked by format header fields, not just magic bytes).

reasons.notAFont: A file named like a font does not have a valid font header.

rules.why: PolinRider, GhostAction and the RMG-Py attacker stored their obfuscated JavaScript loader as `public/fonts/fa-solid-*.woff2`. Nobody reviews binary-looking assets in a diff, and the file is later run with `node`. Combined with any auto-run surface in the same change, this becomes a block.

references.title: OpenSourceMalware: PolinRider dossier and YARA rule
RMG-Py incident report and hardening advice

rules.title: Asset in an execution position
rules.summary: An image or font asset referenced from an execution position (npm script, dev container hook, workflow step, shell script, `fork`, or read and evaluated).

reasons.command: A script or hook runs an image, font or other non-script file with Node.
reasons.fork: Code starts a new Node process from an image or font file.
reasons.evaluated: Code reads an image or font file and builds code from it at runtime.

rules.why: Assets are never code. When something hands an asset to Node, or reads one and passes it to `eval`, `new Function` or `vm`, the asset is a disguised payload. VS Code tasks are covered by DOME-VSC-004.

references.title: OpenSourceMalware: PolinRider dossier and YARA rule
Microsoft: Developer-targeting campaign using malicious Next.js repositories

rules.title: Code after the module body in a config file
rules.summary: Code after the module body in JS/TS config files, especially after a long run of whitespace.

reasons.tail: A config file has code after its export statement.
reasons.paddedTail: A config file has code after its export statement, pushed out of view by a long run of whitespace.

rules.why: PolinRider and the Next.js campaign appended an obfuscated loader to `postcss.config.mjs`, `tailwind.config.js` and `next.config.*`, after `export default` and hundreds of spaces so it sits off-screen in editors and diffs. The build tool then runs it on every `npm run dev`.

references.title: OpenSourceMalware: PolinRider dossier and YARA rule
Microsoft: Developer-targeting campaign using malicious Next.js repositories

rules.title: Whitespace padding or very long line in source
rules.summary: Very long lines or heavy whitespace padding in source and config files.

reasons.padding: A source line has code pushed far to the right by a long run of whitespace.
reasons.longLine: A source file that is otherwise readable has a single extremely long line.

rules.why: Payloads appended to ordinary source files hide past the right edge of the editor or review pane. Minified bundles are expected to have long lines and are skipped by name.

references.title: OpenSourceMalware: PolinRider dossier and YARA rule

rules.title: Runtime code construction in config or route code
rules.summary: Runtime code construction (`eval`, `new Function`, `vm.runIn*`, detached hidden `child_process` spawns) in config or route files.

reasons.eval: A config or route file calls eval.
reasons.function: A config or route file builds a function from a string with Function.
reasons.vm: A config or route file compiles and runs code with the vm module.
reasons.hiddenSpawn: A config or route file starts a detached, hidden background process.

rules.why: Config files and server routes run with full privileges whenever the project builds or starts. Loaders decode a payload and run it with `eval` or `new Function`, or start a detached hidden process that outlives the dev server.

references.title: Microsoft: Developer-targeting campaign using malicious Next.js repositories
OpenSourceMalware: PolinRider dossier and YARA rule

rules.title: Dev container lifecycle command
rules.summary: `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json` `initializeCommand`, `onCreateCommand`, `postCreateCommand`, `postStartCommand` or `postAttachCommand` added or changed.

reasons.hostCommand: The initializeCommand hook runs on the host machine, outside the container, before the container starts.
reasons.lifecycle: A dev container command runs automatically when the container is created, started or attached.
reasons.payload: A dev container command downloads and runs code, or runs a file that is not a script with Node.

rules.why: Dev container hooks run without a prompt when someone opens the repository in a container or a Codespace. `initializeCommand` is the most sensitive: it runs on the host, with access to the developer's keys and wallets.

references.title: Dev Container metadata reference
Microsoft: Developer-targeting campaign using malicious Next.js repositories

rules.title: Encoded URL in .env with code that sends the environment
rules.summary: Base64-encoded URLs in `.env` files combined with code that sends `process.env` over the network.

reasons.encodedUrl: An environment file stores a URL encoded as base64.
reasons.envSent: Code sends the whole process environment over the network.

rules.why: The malicious Next.js repositories Microsoft describes keep their C2 address base64-encoded in `.env` and add a backend route that posts the entire `process.env` (API keys, wallet keys, tokens) to it. Each half alone is a review; together they block.

references.title: Microsoft: Developer-targeting campaign using malicious Next.js repositories

rules.title: Workflow added, changed or risky
rules.summary: New or changed workflow under `.github/workflows/`, weighted up for `pull_request_target`, secrets passed to `curl`/`wget`, or posting to raw IPs.

reasons.changed: A GitHub Actions workflow was added or changed.
reasons.pullRequestTarget: The workflow runs on pull_request_target, with write access and secrets, for pull requests from forks.
reasons.checksOutPrHead: The workflow runs on pull_request_target and checks out the pull request's own code.
reasons.secretsToNetwork: A workflow step sends repository secrets to a network tool.
reasons.rawIp: A workflow step contacts a raw IP address.

rules.why: GhostAction added workflows that read every repository secret and posted them to an attacker server. `pull_request_target` combined with a checkout of the pull request runs untrusted code with write access.

references.title: Socket: GhostAction workflow injection
GitHub Actions security hardening

rules.title: .gitignore stops ignoring .vscode or .env
rules.summary: `.gitignore` change that stops ignoring `.vscode` or `.env`.
rules.why: In the RMG-Py incident and RitualPlay analysis, the attacker edited `.gitignore` so the malicious `.vscode` folder would be committed and pushed to other contributors.

references.title: RMG-Py incident report and hardening advice

rules.title: Git hooks committed to the repository
rules.summary: Git hooks committed to the repo (`.husky/`, `.githooks/`, `simple-git-hooks`) or a `core.hooksPath` setting.

reasons.committedHook: A git hook is committed to the repository and runs on commits, checkouts or pushes once installed.
reasons.hooksPath: A script or config points git at hooks inside the repository with core.hooksPath.

rules.why: Hooks committed to the repository are installed by `npm install` (husky, simple-git-hooks) or by `core.hooksPath`, then run on every commit, checkout or push. A changed hook is an easy place to hide a payload.

references.title: RMG-Py incident report and hardening advice

rules.title: Known-bad file hash
rules.summary: File hashes on the known-bad list (synced from the Dome Registry and public advisories).

reasons.knownHash: This file is byte-for-byte identical to a known malicious file.

rules.why: Campaigns reuse the same loader files across many repositories. An exact hash match needs no interpretation, so it always blocks and cannot be lowered by `.dome.yml`.

references.title: OpenSourceMalware: PolinRider dossier and YARA rule

rules.title: Published campaign marker
rules.summary: Published campaign markers (for example the signatures in OpenSourceMalware's PolinRider YARA rule).

reasons.marker: This file contains a byte sequence published as a marker of a known malware campaign.

rules.why: Obfuscated loaders change their hash on every copy but keep distinctive strings. Markers come from public research and live in `packages/intel` data files, never in rule code.

references.title: OpenSourceMalware: PolinRider dossier and YARA rule

rules.title: Known malicious npm package
rules.summary: Dependencies on known malicious npm packages.

reasons.dependency: package.json depends on a package published as part of a known malware campaign.
reasons.lockfile: The lockfile resolves a package published as part of a known malware campaign.

rules.why: PolinRider published look-alike packages such as `tailwindcss-style-animate` whose install scripts ran the loader. A dependency on one runs it on the next `npm install`, even if it was added deep in the lockfile.

references.title: OpenSourceMalware: PolinRider dossier and YARA rule

rules.title: Known staging or C2 domain in an executable position
rules.summary: Known staging and C2 domains in executable positions (tasks, scripts, hooks, workflows, config and route code).

reasons.domain: Code that runs automatically contacts a domain known to host malware or command-and-control servers.

rules.why: Loaders fetch their second stage from a small set of staging hosts. A known host in a task, script, hook or config file means the repository reaches out to attacker infrastructure.

references.title: OpenSourceMalware: PolinRider dossier and YARA rule
Microsoft: Developer-targeting campaign using malicious Next.js repositories

rules.title: Install script added or changed
rules.summary: `preinstall`, `install`, `postinstall` or `prepare` scripts added or changed (and `binding.gyp`, which npm builds on install).

reasons.installScript: A package.json script that npm runs automatically on install was added or changed.
reasons.nodeGyp: A binding.gyp file makes npm run a native build on install.

rules.why: Install scripts run with the developer's privileges the moment someone types `npm install`. PolinRider shipped through packages such as `tailwindcss-style-animate` whose install hooks ran the loader.

references.title: npm scripts and lifecycle events
OpenSourceMalware: PolinRider dossier and YARA rule

rules.title: Install script runs an unexpected file
rules.summary: An install script runs a file that is not tracked source or a known build output.

reasons.nonScript: An install script runs a file that is not a script (such as a font or image).
reasons.missing: An install script runs a file that is not in the repository and is not a known build output.

rules.why: An honest install hook runs code you can read in the repository (`node scripts/setup.js`) or a build output (`node dist/install.js`). A hook that runs an asset, or a file that only appears after something else downloads it, hides what it does.

references.title: npm scripts and lifecycle events
OpenSourceMalware: PolinRider dossier and YARA rule

rules.title: Propagation script rewrites history
rules.summary: Propagation scripts that rewind the clock, amend the last commit and force-push.

reasons.amendForcePush: A script amends the last commit and force-pushes it.
reasons.rewritesHistory: A script rewinds the clock, amends the last commit and force-pushes, hiding a change inside existing history.

rules.why: PolinRider spread with `temp_auto_push.bat`: it set the system clock back, amended the latest commit to include the payload and force-pushed, so the change appears in an old, already-reviewed commit.

references.title: OpenSourceMalware: PolinRider dossier and YARA rule
RMG-Py incident report and hardening advice

rules.title: Code reads Stellar CLI identities
rules.summary: Code that reads Stellar CLI identities (`~/.config/stellar/identity/*.toml`, plaintext unless created with `--secure-store`).

reasons.reads: Project code refers to the Stellar CLI identity folder, where secret keys are stored.
reasons.exfiltrates: Project code refers to the Stellar CLI identity folder and also makes network requests.

rules.why: Stellar CLI identities are stored as plaintext TOML files containing secret keys unless created with `--secure-store`. A project file has no reason to read them, and code that reads them and talks to the network can drain accounts.

references.title: Stellar CLI key storage

rules.title: Code reads browser wallet extension storage
rules.summary: Code that reads browser wallet extension storage (Freighter and others) from a project file.

reasons.reads: Project code refers to browser extension storage, where wallet extensions keep their vaults.
reasons.exfiltrates: Project code refers to browser extension storage and also makes network requests.

rules.why: Developer-targeting malware collects browser extension storage to steal wallet vaults, including Stellar wallets such as Freighter. Application code never needs to read another extension's storage from disk.

references.title: Microsoft: Developer-targeting campaign using malicious Next.js repositories
Abstract Security: Tracking the VS Code tasks infection vector

rules.title: Hard-coded Stellar secret key
rules.summary: Hard-coded Stellar secret keys (`S…` strkeys with a valid checksum) committed to the repo.

reasons.secretKey: A Stellar secret key is committed to the repository.

rules.why: Anyone who can read the repository can sign for the account. Only candidates with a valid SEP-23 checksum are reported, so random 56-character strings do not match.

references.title: SEP-23: Strkey encoding

rules.title: Task runs on folder open
rules.summary: A `.vscode/tasks.json` or `*.code-workspace` task sets `runOptions.runOn` to `folderOpen`.

reasons.folderOpen: A VS Code task is set to run automatically when the folder is opened.

rules.why: A folder-open task runs as soon as someone opens the repository in VS Code or Cursor and trusts the workspace. It was the entry point in PolinRider/TasksJacker, Contagious Interview and the RMG-Py incident, where the task launched a script disguised as a font.

references.title: Abstract Security: Tracking the VS Code tasks infection vector
OpenSourceMalware: PolinRider dossier and YARA rule
RMG-Py incident report and hardening advice
VS Code Workspace Trust

rules.title: Automatic tasks turned on
rules.summary: Workspace settings set `task.allowAutomaticTasks` to `on`.

reasons.allowAutomaticTasks: Turns on automatic tasks so VS Code does not ask first.

rules.why: VS Code asks before running a folder-open task for the first time. Setting `task.allowAutomaticTasks` to `on` in the workspace removes that prompt, which is what the RMG-Py attacker did alongside the malicious task.

references.title: RMG-Py incident report and hardening advice
VS Code Workspace Trust

rules.title: .vscode hidden from view
rules.summary: `files.exclude` or `search.exclude` hides `.vscode` or `tasks.json`.

reasons.hidden: Workspace settings hide the .vscode folder or tasks.json from the file explorer or search.

rules.why: Hiding `.vscode` keeps a malicious task out of sight in the editor. The RMG-Py attacker added `files.exclude` entries for exactly this.

references.title: RMG-Py incident report and hardening advice

rules.title: Task runs a non-script file with Node
rules.summary: A task command runs a font, image or other non-script file with `node` (string or array form, `sh -c`, `-r`/`--import`, stdin).

reasons.nonScript: A VS Code task runs a file that is not a script (such as a font or image) with Node.
reasons.nonScriptViaNpm: A VS Code task runs an npm script that runs a file that is not a script with Node.

rules.why: Legitimate tasks run JavaScript files. Running `node` on a `.woff2`, `.png` or similar is how PolinRider, GhostAction and the RMG-Py attacker hid their loader: the "font" is really obfuscated JavaScript.

references.title: OpenSourceMalware: PolinRider dossier and YARA rule
RMG-Py incident report and hardening advice
Abstract Security: Tracking the VS Code tasks infection vector

rules.title: Task downloads and runs code
rules.summary: A task command downloads and pipes to a shell (`curl … | sh`, `wget … | bash`, PowerShell `iwr | iex`).

reasons.downloadAndRun: A VS Code task downloads something from the network and runs it.

rules.why: Contagious Interview and Microsoft's Next.js report describe tasks that fetch a second stage from a staging server and run it in a shell. Nothing about the downloaded code is visible in the repository.

references.title: Abstract Security: Tracking the VS Code tasks infection vector
Microsoft: Developer-targeting campaign using malicious Next.js repositories

rules.title: Task output hidden
rules.summary: Task options hide output (`presentation.reveal: never`, `presentation.echo: false`, `hide: true`) on a task that also runs on folder open or runs a payload.

reasons.hiddenOutput: The task hides its terminal output, so nothing is visible while it runs.

rules.why: Malicious folder-open tasks set `reveal: never` so no terminal panel appears. On its own this is harmless; it is reported as context next to other task findings.

references.title: Abstract Security: Tracking the VS Code tasks infection vector
OpenSourceMalware: PolinRider dossier and YARA rule
